Salt of the Covenant
sawlt uhv thuh KUHV-uh-nuhnt
noun
From Leviticus 2:13; the salt commanded with every offering, a token of the perpetual covenant.

📖 Biblical Definition

The salt of the covenant is the salt which the LORD commanded to be offered with every sacrifice: with all thine offerings thou shalt offer salt; neither shalt thou suffer the salt of the covenant of thy God to be lacking from thy meat offering. Salt, which preserves from corruption and does not itself decay, was the fitting token of the covenant’s perpetuity and incorruptibility. So the LORD speaks of His covenant with the priesthood as a covenant of salt for ever, and of the kingdom given to David as a covenant of salt—an everlasting, unbreakable bond. To eat salt with another was, in the East, to enter a sacred bond of fellowship and fidelity. The salt upon the offerings declared that the worshipper drew near in covenant, and that the covenant of God endures and preserves. The figure is taken up by the Lord, who calls His disciples the salt of the earth, and bids them have salt in themselves, and be at peace one with another. The dictionary honors the salt of the covenant as a token of the perpetuity and incorruptibility of God’s covenant with His people, a witness that the bond He makes does not decay, and a call to the covenant fidelity, purity, and preserving witness that the salt signifies—that the people of His covenant are to be themselves a savour of incorruption in a perishing world.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The salt commanded with every offering, a token of the perpetual, incorruptible covenant; God’s bond that does not decay, and a call to covenant fidelity and witness.

SALT OF THE COVENANT, the salt offered with every sacrifice (Lev 2:13).

Salt preserves and does not decay—a token of the covenant’s perpetuity.

The LORD’s covenants of priesthood and kingdom called covenants of salt.

📖 Key Scripture

Lev 2:13 — "And every oblation of thy meat offering shalt thou season with salt; neither shalt thou suffer the salt of the covenant of thy God to be lacking from thy meat offering: with all thine offerings thou shalt offer salt."

Num 18:19 — "All the heave offerings of the holy things, which the children of Israel offer unto the LORD, have I given thee, and thy sons and thy daughters with thee, by a statute for ever: it is a covenant of salt for ever before the LORD unto thee and to thy seed with thee."

2Ch 13:5 — "Ought ye not to know that the LORD God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?"

Mar 9:50 — "Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his saltness, wherewith will ye season it? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace one with another."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The salt is dismissed as quaint ritual detail; Scripture makes it a token of the covenant’s perpetuity and a call to incorruptible covenant fidelity.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption is the dismissal of the salt as quaint ritual detail—a culinary footnote in the sacrificial law, easily passed over. But the LORD invested it with covenant meaning: it is the salt of the covenant of thy God (Lev 2:13), and He speaks of His abiding bonds as covenants of salt for ever (Num 18:19; 2 Chr 13:5). Salt preserves from corruption and does not itself decay; it is therefore the fit token of a covenant that endures and cannot be broken.

The principle to recover is the perpetuity and incorruptibility of God’s covenant, and the covenant fidelity it summons in His people. The bond God makes does not decay; His covenant of salt stands for ever, a comfort to all who rest in His unbreakable promise. And the figure passes to the disciple: Christ calls His people the salt of the earth, and bids them have salt in themselves, and have peace one with another (Mark 9:50). The people of the covenant are to be themselves a savour of incorruption—faithful, pure, preserving—in a perishing world, lest the salt lose its saltness and be good for nothing. The salt of the covenant is thus both promise and charge: God’s bond endures; let His people be true to it.
